resources.string: Connect an AI service, then choose the model MiniRP will use for chats and preset setup.
A provider is the service that runs your model. Choose its template to fill in the connection details. If the service needs an API key, get it from the provider’s website.
Pick a model from %1$s to use for your first conversations.
Check the API address and key, then try again. If your provider doesn’t list models, enter the exact model ID from its website.

Thinking effort is how much time your AI spends working things out before it replies. For a complicated story or a plugin, start with the highest level. For a quick chat, try a lower one. Higher levels can take longer and use more of your plan’s quota. You can change this anytime in Settings → Models.
Copy this prompt into %1$s, then follow the steps it gives you.
I’m new to MiniRP for Android. Please reply in %1$s. My device region is %2$s. First read the official MiniRP guide at %3$s. Let me know if you can’t open it.

Help me choose and connect a model provider. Ask where I’ll use it, what I want to do, and my budget. Explain how to create an account and find an API key. Give me the exact MiniRP values for provider template or name, protocol, API address (Base URL), and a starter model ID. MiniRP supports OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, Google Gemini, and Ollama. Walk me through Add provider, Save, and choosing a model.

Help me decide whether to set up web search (real_search) and page fetch (real_fetch) in MiniRP for Android. Under Settings → Search and fetch APIs, I can choose each provider separately and enter its key. Search supports DeepSeek, Tavily, Exa, and Brave Search. Fetch supports DeepSeek, Tavily, and Exa. When DeepSeek is selected, MiniRP can reuse the key from a saved DeepSeek model provider. Without a search key, MiniRP tries Mwmbl and then the built-in browser. The browser can also fetch pages. Search the web for current official documentation and reviews from developers. Recommend options for my account and region, then show how to test search and fetch using a public page.

Use live web searches for every recommendation, and ask me to enable browsing if you can’t access the web. Compare one or two suitable services using current official pricing, subscriptions, and API integration docs, plus recent first-hand experiences from developers who actually integrated them. Consider well-reviewed coding plans, agent plans, and AI subscriptions that include direct API access. Check which options are available in my region. For any such plan you recommend, check whether its terms allow API access from a third-party client such as MiniRP, whether its endpoints support the feature I’m setting up, and what usage limits and overage charges apply. Distinguish official terms from user reports. Explain free and paid options, regional availability, any API credits included in a subscription, and separate pay-as-you-go charges. Link the official sources and developer discussions you checked and give their dates. Give the steps in plain language, one at a time.
Ask me to enter secrets only in the provider’s website or in MiniRP. Never ask me to send you API keys, verification codes, or payment details.
